name: Beypore Uru (traditional wooden shipbuilding)
tagline: Living maritime craft — handcrafted urus, stories and waterfront visits
summary: Beypore’s uru shipyards keep a 1,500‑year wooden shipbuilding tradition alive; visitors can watch skilled khalasis and maistries at work, learn stories of Gulf trade, and combine a shipyard visit…
description: Beypore’s uru building is a living maritime craft: large wooden dhows (urus) are hand‑made by master carpenters (odaiyis/maistries) and khalasis using techniques passed down through generations. The craft connects the town to centuries of trade with the Arab world and remains visible along the Chaliyar estuary and the Kakkadath–BC Road shipyards.

The industry matters as cultural heritage, local livelihood and a tourism draw. Recent destination work and funding aim to link traditional shipbuilding with responsible tourism so visitors can experience the craft while the community benefits from guided visits, storytelling and local craft sales.

A visitor to Beypore typically sees hull framing and finishing from safe vantage points, may meet craftsmen if permission is granted, and can add a short visit to Beypore beach, the fishing harbour and the nearby lighthouse. Yard entry is not automatic — most shipyards are working, privately owned sites and access depends on the builders or arranged tours (confirm before you travel).
highlights: A continuous shipbuilding tradition of over a millennium, centred on handcrafted urus

sections.heading: Background
body: Beypore sits at the mouth of the Chaliyar River and is the principal centre for the uru (a large dhow‑type wooden ship) in Kerala. The craft uses inherited, non‑plan based skills: master carpenters (odaiyis) and khalasis build the hull and outfit vessels for Gulf and other clients.

Organisations and local tourism bodies have been working to conserve and promote the uru as living heritage; the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) has pursued protective measures including a Geographical Indication application (filed 08‑12‑2022, status listed as pre‑examination on the IP India registry).

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: From public vantage points and authorized visits you can watch frames being assembled, steaming and shaping of timbers, caulking and joinery — the most photogenic and instructive moments are hull framing and the finishing stages. Builders sometimes demonstrate traditional tools and explain craft terms; respectful conversation and small donations for demonstrations are common.

Combine a shipyard viewing with the short walk to Beypore Beach, the fishing harbour and the lighthouse. Look for the local Dhow Museum and responsible‑tourism units that offer storytelling, short guided walks and craft demonstrations that contextualise the shipyards for visitors.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Shipyards are working industrial sites: you usually view activity from outside or on arranged visits. Contact DTPC Kozhikode or a local tour operator to request a guided yard visit or workshop; ask for permission in advance and reconfirm on arrival. Expect activity to be intermittent — urus are built to order and major work shows up during specific contracts.

Travel logistics: Beypore is about 10 km south of Kozhikode city (rail and bus connections). Calicut/Calicut International Airport (Karipur) is roughly 22–25 km by road (allow extra time). Local taxis, autorickshaws and buses connect Kozhikode and Beypore.

latest.text: Kerala declares Beypore an International Responsible Tourism Destination to strengthen links between traditional industries (including uru shipbuilding) and tourism.
Kerala state budget 2026–27 allocates Rs 5 crore to the 'Beypore Uru Tourism Project' to support destination development and connect uru building with tourism initiatives.
A 'Good Practice' story documents Beypore’s restoration and promotion of uru building as community heritage and a responsible‑tourism asset.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–March (post‑monsoon dry season; yard activity and festivals peak in this period)
visitorInfo.howToReach: Beypore is about 10 km south of Kozhikode city. Kozhikode Railway Station and the city bus stand serve the area; Calicut/Calicut International Airport (Karipur) is roughly 22–25 km by road. Local taxis, autos and buses connect the station/airport to Beypore; arrange guided yard visits through DTPC or a trusted operator.
etiquette: Shipyards are working sites — always ask permission before entering; many yards allow viewing only with prior arrangement.
Wear sturdy closed shoes and keep a safe distance from active work; follow all instructions from yard staff.
Photograph respectfully and only after checking with craftsmen; small gratuities for demonstrations are appreciated.
Confirm visits in advance with DTPC Kozhikode or a local responsible‑tourism unit — activity is intermittent and often linked to specific orders.
